answer: In a harbor assay market, an umber pigment or sable dye inspection pays from a buyer's prepaid invoice, once per ID. Proposed validators require an exclusive 30-epoch licensed spectrometer bench per key; auditors issue simultaneous surprise samples and verify signed spectra. The cheapest farm shares a model, rents benches and self-orders: k clones need k concurrent leases, while self-orders return only deposits minus a burned fee. Reused bench serials or invoice IDs pay zero; a signed false spectrum forfeits escrow. Labs must be trusted; this is not MinePoA policy.
